changes: Keep listOperations active-only. Store at most 500 display-only closed snapshots in existing IndexedDB meta; archive and active deletion commit in the same transaction for acknowledgement, explicit unknown closure, legacy closure and capacity collection. No schema migration or operation-store change.

Display active plus closed rows by createdAt descending with deterministic ID tie-break and complete local date/time. Keep open links and unresolved active queries; no acknowledgement/bulk-clear controls or state. Closed unknown rows never query or restart recovery.

History snapshots contain only operation ID/method/state/time/thread/project/destination IDs and closure reason. No request/result/error bodies, draft identities, resource paths, terminal ownership/results or emergency snapshots.

History damage preserves valid bounded rows and emits a separate history warning without blocking active recovery or archival. True IndexedDB write/commit failures still roll back archive and deletion. Already-acknowledged malformed legacy records are best-effort history only; unacknowledged legacy identity/proof validation stays strict.

At active pressure (160), archive oldest eligible records toward 128: not_sent, consumed accepted, or ordinary accepted without thread/typed-owner handoff. Keep ordinary limit 200 and reserved emergency slot 201. Preserve unresolved and unconsumed target receipts; history budget does not consume active capacity.

Loaded matching legacy target receipts can become consumed while preserving legacy drafts; ordinary queried/migrated acceptance can age out under pressure. Terminal/open and system/recover retain owner-specific proof until explicit owner handling.
